subproblem.title: Gram determinant of two linear functionals restricted to a 2-plane (Lagrange identity + Parseval)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, T a linear subspace of ℝ^P with dim T = 2, (u_i)_{i ∈ Fin(dim T)} := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T (vectors of T viewed in ℝ^P), p_T := T.starProjection, and p, q ∈ ℝ^P. Let G be the dim T × dim T matrix G_ij := ⟨p,u_i⟩⟨p,u_j⟩ + ⟨q,u_i⟩⟨q,u_j⟩. Then det G = |p_T p|²·|p_T q|² − ⟨p_T p, p_T q⟩².
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (T : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (p q : Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ T = 2 → Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ T) => inner ℝ p (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T i : Euclid P) * inner ℝ p (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T j : Euclid P) + inner ℝ q (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T i : Euclid P) * inner ℝ q (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T j : Euclid P)) = ‖T.starProjection p‖ ^ 2 * ‖T.starProjection q‖ ^ 2 - inner ℝ (T.starProjection p) (T.starProjection q) ^ 2
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4 and 5 (Gram determinant, Lagrange's identity, Parseval in T) of the parent-supplied proof, stated for arbitrary vectors p, q in place of x̂ and g. Notation: u_i := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T i ∈ T for i ∈ Fin(dim T), p_T := T.starProjection, and P_T := T.orthogonalProjectionOnto : ℝ^P → T, so that (P_T v : ℝ^P) = p_T v (`Submodule.coe_orthogonalProjectionOnto_apply`).
1. (Lagrange's identity on the 2×2 index type.) Claim: for every n ∈ ℕ with n = 2 and all f, g : Fin n → ℝ, det[f_i f_j + g_i g_j]_{i,j ∈ Fin n} = (Σ_i f_i²)(Σ_i g_i²) − (Σ_i f_i g_i)². Proof: n is a variable, so substitute n = 2. Expand the determinant with `Matrix.det_fin_two` and the sums with `Fin.sum_univ_two`. The left side is (f₀² + g₀²)(f₁² + g₁²) − (f₀f₁ + g₀g₁)(f₁f₀ + g₁g₀), the right side is (f₀² + f₁²)(g₀² + g₁²) − (f₀g₀ + f₁g₁)², and both equal (f₀g₁ − f₁g₀)² (`ring`). Apply the claim with n := dim T (= 2 by hypothesis), f_i := ⟨p,u_i⟩ and g_i := ⟨q,u_i⟩; G is exactly the matrix [f_i f_j + g_i g_j]. This avoids rewriting the dependent index type Fin(dim T). Hence det G = (Σ_i ⟨p,u_i⟩²)(Σ_i ⟨q,u_i⟩²) − (Σ_i ⟨p,u_i⟩⟨q,u_i⟩)².
2. (Reduction to T.) Let v ∈ ℝ^P and i be given. Since u_i ∈ T and v − p_T v ⊥ T (`Submodule.starProjection_inner_eq_zero`), ⟨v,u_i⟩ = ⟨p_T v, u_i⟩. The inner product of T is the restriction of that of ℝ^P (`Submodule.coe_inner`), so this equals ⟨P_T v, u_i⟩_T.
3. (Parseval in T.) (u_i) is an orthonormal basis of the inner product space T. Hence for y, z ∈ T: Σ_i ⟨y,u_i⟩² = |y|² (`OrthonormalBasis.sum_sq_inner_left`), and Σ_i ⟨y,u_i⟩⟨u_i,z⟩ = ⟨y,z⟩ (`OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner`). By symmetry ⟨u_i,z⟩ = ⟨z,u_i⟩ (`real_inner_comm`), so Σ_i ⟨y,u_i⟩⟨z,u_i⟩ = ⟨y,z⟩.
4. (The three sums.) By steps 2 and 3 with y := P_T p and z := P_T q:
   Σ_i ⟨p,u_i⟩² = |P_T p|²;
   Σ_i ⟨q,u_i⟩² = |P_T q|²;
   Σ_i ⟨p,u_i⟩⟨q,u_i⟩ = ⟨P_T p, P_T q⟩_T.
   Norms and inner products in T are those of the underlying vectors in ℝ^P (`Submodule.norm_coe`, `Submodule.coe_inner`), and (P_T v : ℝ^P) = p_T v. So these equal |p_T p|², |p_T q|² and ⟨p_T p, p_T q⟩.
5. (Conclusion.) Substituting step 4 into step 1 gives det G = |p_T p|²·|p_T q|² − ⟨p_T p, p_T q⟩². ∎
proof_key_steps: Lagrange's identity on Fin n with n = 2: det[f_i f_j + g_i g_j] = (Σf_i²)(Σg_i²) − (Σf_i g_i)² (subst n, Matrix.det_fin_two, Fin.sum_univ_two, ring); apply with n = dim T.
⟨v,u_i⟩ = ⟨p_T v, u_i⟩ = ⟨P_T v, u_i⟩_T because v − p_T v ⊥ T ∋ u_i.
Parseval in T (sum_sq_inner_left, sum_inner_mul_inner) gives Σ⟨p,u_i⟩² = |p_T p|², Σ⟨q,u_i⟩² = |p_T q|², Σ⟨p,u_i⟩⟨q,u_i⟩ = ⟨p_T p, p_T q⟩.

subproblem.title: Derivative of the polar map y ↦ (|y|, arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩)) at a point x with ⟨x,a⟩ ≠ 0
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and a, e, x ∈ ℝ^P with ⟨x,a⟩ ≠ 0 (no orthonormality of a, e is assumed). Put F̃(y) := (|y|, arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩)) ∈ ℝ × ℝ. Then for every v ∈ ℝ^P the Fréchet derivative of F̃ at x (fderiv ℝ F̃ x) satisfies DF̃(x)v = (⟨x,v⟩/|x|, ⟨⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a, v⟩/(⟨x,a⟩² + ⟨x,e⟩²)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (a e x : Euclid P), inner ℝ x a ≠ 0 → ∀ v : Euclid P, fderiv ℝ (fun y : Euclid P => (‖y‖, Real.arctan (inner ℝ y e / inner ℝ y a))) x v = (inner ℝ x v / ‖x‖, inner ℝ (inner ℝ x a • e - inner ℝ x e • a) v / (inner ℝ x a ^ 2 + inner ℝ x e ^ 2))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 (F3) of the parent-supplied proof, stated for general a, e with ⟨x,a⟩ ≠ 0. Notation: α := ⟨x,a⟩ ≠ 0, β := ⟨x,e⟩, ρ := α² + β², A := αe − βa, F̃(y) := (|y|, arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩)).
1. (Non-degeneracy.) x ≠ 0, since otherwise α = ⟨0,a⟩ = 0. Hence |x| > 0. Also ρ ≥ α² > 0, so ρ ≠ 0.
2. (Norm.) The map y ↦ |y|² has derivative v ↦ 2⟨x,v⟩ at x (`hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq` and `HasStrictFDerivAt.hasFDerivAt`: derivative 2 • innerSL ℝ x). Its value |x|² at x is nonzero, so by the chain rule for the square root (`HasFDerivAt.sqrt`), y ↦ sqrt(|y|²) has derivative v ↦ (1/(2·sqrt(|x|²)))·2⟨x,v⟩ at x. Since sqrt(|y|²) = |y| for every y (`Real.sqrt_sq`, because |y| ≥ 0), the norm y ↦ |y| has this same derivative at x. As sqrt(|x|²) = |x|, its value at v is ⟨x,v⟩/|x|.
3. (Linear coordinates.) By symmetry of the real inner product (`real_inner_comm`), y ↦ ⟨y,e⟩ equals the continuous linear map innerSL ℝ e : y ↦ ⟨e,y⟩. So it has derivative v ↦ ⟨e,v⟩ at x (`ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt`). Likewise y ↦ ⟨y,a⟩ has derivative v ↦ ⟨a,v⟩ at x. Transfer along the pointwise identities with `HasFDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq`.
4. (Reciprocal.) t ↦ t⁻¹ has derivative −(α²)⁻¹ at t = α ≠ 0 (`hasFDerivAt_inv`). By the chain rule (`HasFDerivAt.comp`) and step 3, y ↦ ⟨y,a⟩⁻¹ has derivative v ↦ −⟨a,v⟩/α² at x.
5. (Product.) By the product rule (`HasFDerivAt.fun_mul`) and steps 3–4, q(y) := ⟨y,e⟩·⟨y,a⟩⁻¹ has derivative v ↦ β·(−⟨a,v⟩/α²) + α⁻¹·⟨e,v⟩ at x.
6. (Arctan.) arctan has derivative t ↦ 1/(1 + t²) (`HasFDerivAt.arctan`), and q(x) = β·α⁻¹. So y ↦ arctan(q(y)) has derivative v ↦ (1/(1 + (βα⁻¹)²))·(α⁻¹⟨e,v⟩ − β⟨a,v⟩/α²) at x.
7. (Pair and identification.) By `HasFDerivAt.prodMk` and steps 2 and 6, G(y) := (|y|, arctan(q(y))) has at x the derivative L : v ↦ (⟨x,v⟩·(1/(2·sqrt(|x|²)))·2, (1/(1 + (βα⁻¹)²))·(α⁻¹⟨e,v⟩ − β⟨a,v⟩/α²)). For every y, ⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩ = ⟨y,e⟩·⟨y,a⟩⁻¹ (`div_eq_mul_inv`, which holds even when ⟨y,a⟩ = 0). So F̃ = G everywhere, and F̃ also has derivative L at x (`HasFDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq`). By uniqueness of the Fréchet derivative (`HasFDerivAt.fderiv`), fderiv ℝ F̃ x = L.
8. (Simplification.) Fix v. First coordinate: with sqrt(|x|²) = |x| (`Real.sqrt_sq`, |x| ≥ 0), ⟨x,v⟩·(1/(2|x|))·2 = ⟨x,v⟩/|x| since |x| ≠ 0. Second coordinate: 1/(1 + β²/α²) = α²/ρ. Hence (α²/ρ)·(⟨e,v⟩/α − β⟨a,v⟩/α²) = (α⟨e,v⟩ − β⟨a,v⟩)/ρ, using α ≠ 0 and ρ ≠ 0 (`field_simp`, `ring`). Finally ⟨A,v⟩ = ⟨αe − βa, v⟩ = α⟨e,v⟩ − β⟨a,v⟩ (`inner_sub_left`, `real_inner_smul_left`). Therefore fderiv ℝ F̃ x v = (⟨x,v⟩/|x|, ⟨⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a, v⟩/(⟨x,a⟩² + ⟨x,e⟩²)), as claimed. ∎
proof_key_steps: The norm is sqrt(|y|²), so its derivative at x is v ↦ ⟨x,v⟩/|x| (hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq, HasFDerivAt.sqrt, Real.sqrt_sq).
y ↦ ⟨y,e⟩·⟨y,a⟩⁻¹ is differentiated by the linear-map, inverse, chain and product rules; arctan is then applied (HasFDerivAt.arctan).
Pair with HasFDerivAt.prodMk, then transfer from ⟨y,e⟩·⟨y,a⟩⁻¹ to ⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩ with congr_of_eventuallyEq and take HasFDerivAt.fderiv.
Field arithmetic: the coordinates are ⟨x,v⟩/|x| and (⟨x,a⟩⟨e,v⟩ − ⟨x,e⟩⟨a,v⟩)/ρ = ⟨⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a, v⟩/ρ.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches the prose. The eight-step proof derives all required nonzero denominators, correctly differentiates the norm and angle, pairs the derivatives, and simplifies to the stated formula. No orthonormality assumption or circular reliance is needed.

subproblem.title: Squared norm of the orthogonal projection onto a 2-plane spanned by an orthonormal pair
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P with dim Q = 2, a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a,e⟩ = 0, and x ∈ ℝ^P. Then |Q.starProjection x|² = ⟨x,a⟩² + ⟨x,e⟩².
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e x : Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → a ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → ‖Q.starProjection x‖ ^ 2 = inner ℝ x a ^ 2 + inner ℝ x e ^ 2
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (F1) of the parent-supplied proof. Notation: α := ⟨x,a⟩, β := ⟨x,e⟩, π := Q.starProjection.
1. (Orthonormality.) ⟨a,a⟩ = |a|² = 1 and ⟨e,e⟩ = |e|² = 1 (`real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq`), and ⟨e,a⟩ = ⟨a,e⟩ = 0 (`real_inner_comm`). So the family (a, e), indexed by Fin 2 as ![a, e], is orthonormal (`orthonormal_iff_ite`, checking the four index pairs). Hence it is linearly independent (`Orthonormal.linearIndependent`).
2. (span{a,e} = Q.) span{a,e} ⊆ Q because a, e ∈ Q (`Submodule.span_le`). The finite dimension of span{a,e} is 2, the size of the linearly independent family (`finrank_span_eq_card`), which equals dim Q. So span{a,e} = Q (`Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq`).
3. (πx = αa + βe.) Put w₀ := αa + βe ∈ Q (Q is a subspace containing a and e). Let w ∈ Q. By step 2, w = c₀a + c₁e for some reals c₀, c₁ (`Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun`, `Fin.sum_univ_two`). Then ⟨x − w₀, a⟩ = α − α⟨a,a⟩ − β⟨e,a⟩ = α − α − 0 = 0. Likewise ⟨x − w₀, e⟩ = β − α⟨a,e⟩ − β⟨e,e⟩ = β − 0 − β = 0. Hence ⟨x − w₀, w⟩ = c₀·0 + c₁·0 = 0. By the characterization of the orthogonal projection (`Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero`: if w₀ ∈ Q and x − w₀ ⊥ Q, then πx = w₀), πx = w₀.
4. (Norm.) Write |πx|² = ⟨w₀, w₀⟩ (`real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq`). Expand bilinearly: α²⟨a,a⟩ + αβ⟨a,e⟩ + βα⟨e,a⟩ + β²⟨e,e⟩ = α² + β², by step 1. So |Q.starProjection x|² = ⟨x,a⟩² + ⟨x,e⟩². ∎
proof_key_steps: (a, e) is orthonormal, hence linearly independent; span{a,e} ⊆ Q has dimension 2 = dim Q, so span{a,e} = Q.
w₀ := ⟨x,a⟩a + ⟨x,e⟩e ∈ Q and x − w₀ ⊥ a, e, hence ⊥ Q; so Q.starProjection x = w₀ (eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero).

audit.reason: All hypotheses appear in both prose and the one-line type. The proof establishes orthonormality, identifies the span with Q by dimension, characterizes the projection by orthogonality, and expands its squared norm. Each step is justified and non-circular.
